Caral stands on a dry terrace above the green Supe River valley. The archaeological complex is associated with one of the oldest civilizations in the Americas. Its surviving monumental buildings offer a glimpse into the layout of an early urban center long before the time of the Incas.

The site is part of the UNESCO World Heritage List. Visitors can explore the stone structures and see how they fit into the open coastal landscape. Caral adds a much earlier chapter of history to a journey through Peru than Cusco and Machu Picchu, revealing the deep roots of urban settlements in the country.

The long river journey toward Angel Falls begins on the Carrao. Travelers follow the river in motorized curiaras, narrow traditional boats. Forested banks and stretches of savanna alternate along the way before towering cliffs come into view.

The Carrao itinerary includes going ashore and walking across the savanna. The route then continues along the narrower Churún River. Passage through some sections depends on the water level.

## Chalchuapa's Early Ceremonial Center

Casa Blanca Archaeological Park is in [Chalchuapa](/el-salvador/place/chalchuapa/), in the department of Santa Ana. Today's park preserves part of a much larger ancient settlement. Together with the neighboring El Trapiche area, this district was an important center in the region's early Maya history.

The park contains pre-Columbian mounds and excavated structures. The main ceremonial center later shifted to [Tazumal](/el-salvador/place/tazumal/), so visiting both sites helps explain the development of the ancient city.

## The Museum and Indigo

The Casa Blanca Museum occupies a building with an inner courtyard and covered galleries. Among its exhibits is a fragment of a stela bearing Maya script. An archaeological window reveals the sequence of natural and cultural layers, including a layer of volcanic ash.

Another theme of the park is the traditional indigo dye known as añil in El Salvador. Visitors can learn about methods of dyeing textiles. The opportunity to see the workshop in action depends on the visit program.

## Casa Blanca on an Ada Tours Itinerary

On the [“Best of El Salvador” tour](/el-salvador/tour/el-salvador-san-salvador-suchitoto-gulf-of-fonseca/), Casa Blanca is visited on day three, after Tazumal. The route then continues to Santa Ana and Ataco.
